subject: Renewal: Delta Health hosted API — flexible bands & uplift guardrails
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@deltahealth.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@deltahealth.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: committed usage & uplift caps

Hi Vivek,

Hope you had a good week. Our renewal is coming up and procurement asked me to confirm a few things before we schedule the final review:

1) Usage right-sizing: our actual hosted API consumption for the last 12 months is ~45% of the committed monthly baseline in our current contract. We expect growth but not at the pace we originally forecasted. Can we structure the renewal so the base commit is lower with predictable overage pricing?

2) Uplift guardrail: procurement wants a hard cap on how much Redwood can increase the committed baseline at renewal (we prefer <=10% YoY); they need a number we can put in their renewal checklist.

3) Flexible bands: would Redwood consider a banded per-token pricing approach (e.g., preferential per-token rates for steady overages vs. short spikes) so our unit economics improve with predictable higher volume but we aren’t locked into a large upfront commit?

Can you sketch options or send a short proposal we can circulate with procurement and finance? We need to present options to our CFO by 7/8.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Nguyen
Head of ML Platform, Delta Health
[sara.nguyen@deltahealth.ai]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@deltahealth.ai>
Cc: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@deltahealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: committed usage & uplift caps

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a short proposal (Redwood_Renewal_Proposal_Q3_2026.pdf) with two practical paths that balance predictability for you and economic incentives for higher steady usage. High level:

Option A — Right-size + Quarterly true-up
- Lower base monthly commit to 60% of current
- Quarterly true-up (no financial penalty, just invoice true-up)
- Per-token list: $0.00012/token; committed-tier discount: 18% on tokens used up to commit

Option B — Flex bands (recommended for spiky but growing usage)
- Base commit = 60% of current
- Band 1 (0–100% of commit): $0.00011/token
- Band 2 (100–150% of commit): $0.000095/token (improves unit economics for sustained overage)
- Band 3 (150%+): capped at $0.00009/token for sustained months (requires review if >3 consecutive months)
- Quarterly true-up with automatic smoothing: first month overage in a quarter billed as overage; sustained overage credited into next quarter’s commit calculation.

Uplift guardrail proposal
- Redwood will cap allowed contract renewal uplift to 12% YoY by default for this renewal cycle if Delta signs the flex bands structure.
- Single exception clause: material product pricing changes (e.g., new tokens-based features) will be discussed in advance.

Concessions to help close
- One-time onboarding credit of $20,000 applied toward first-month overage if you accept the Flex bands.
- Priority slot for Dedicated capacity consult (if Delta wants to evaluate reserved capacity in 2027).

I attached the PDF with the numbers and an example year-1 true-up calculation. If you want procurement-friendly language around the uplift cap we can commit to a 12% clause in the SOW.

Can we lock a 30-minute call Wednesday 7/1 to walk procurement through the math?

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189
[Attachment: Redwood_Renewal_Proposal_Q3_2026.pdf]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: Delta Health hosted API — negotiation plan

Team — quick internal note pulled from the call notes and Sara’s asks. Strategy recommendation:

- Accept Flex bands (Option B) but move the uplift cap to 10% (vs my initial 12%) to hit procurement ask and speed to signature.
- In exchange we hold per-token floors as proposed and keep quarterly true-up + $20k one-time credit.
- Watch for legal ask on "renewal uplift" definition — make sure it's annualized baseline not cumulative multi-year.
- If finance pushes back on 10% we keep 12% and offer an incremental 30-day price-protection window post-renewal.

If agreed, I’ll send an updated SOW with the 10% uplift cap and the DocuSign link.

-V

From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@deltahealth.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@deltahealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Delta Health hosted API — flexible bands & uplift guardrails

Vivek — thanks for the options and the call earlier. Procurement did a quick pass and asked two clarifications:

1) Uplift cap: can Redwood commit to a 10% YoY renewal uplift cap (we understand exceptions for new product tiers but need a hard number in the schedule).

2) Per-token floor: procurement wants an explicit floor, i.e., the per-token price should never go above $0.00013/token in any banded scenario (they consider $0.00013 the effective ceiling). Can Redwood agree to include that ceiling in the SOW?

If you can confirm those two items and send us the SOW/DocuSign by EOD 7/6, procurement will sign and we can meet the CFO timeline.

Thanks,
Sara

On Wed, Jul 1, 2026 at 09:12 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sara — we can do the flex bands and the quarterly true-up. Attached is the PDF with numbers.
>
> -V

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@deltahealth.ai>
Cc: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@deltahealth.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Delta Health hosted API — flexible bands & uplift guardrails

Sara — appreciate the clarity. Summary of agreed items below; final SOW and DocuSign link attached.

Agreed commercial points (to be reflected in SOW / schedule):
- Base commit: 60% of your current monthly baseline (explicit line item in SOW).
- Flex bands: Band 1 (0–100%): $0.00011/token; Band 2 (100–150%): $0.000095/token; Band 3 (150%+ sustained): $0.00009/token (subject to review if >3 consecutive months).
- Per-token ceiling (procurement request): Redwood confirms per-token ceiling of $0.00013/token (SOW language added).
- Uplift guardrail: Redwood accepts a 10% YoY maximum renewal commit increase for the next renewal cycle (exclusions for material new product features called out).
- True-up cadence: Quarterly; smoothing applied as described in the proposal.
- One-time credit: $20,000 applied to initial overage billing on month 1.

Next steps:
1) SOW (SOW_DeltaHealth_v2.docx) and the commercial schedule updated with the 10% uplift cap attached.
2) DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/en/sign/abc123-delta-renewal
3) Procurement to sign by EOD 7/6 to meet your CFO timeline; Redwood to execute signature on receipt.
4) Target kickoff for implementation and technical onboarding: July 20, 2026.

If that reads correctly, please confirm and I’ll route the DocuSign. Happy to hop on a 15-min call if procurement wants a line-by-line walk.

Thanks — excited to keep building with Delta Health.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
